def test_vector_function_workers_parameter():
    """Test that VectorFunction accepts and handles the workers parameter correctly."""
    
    # Define a simple vector function
    def vector_func(x):
        return np.array([x[0]**2 + x[1], x[0] * x[1]])
    
    # Test data
    x0 = np.array([1.0, 2.0])
    
    # Test with workers=None (default behavior) - using callable hessian
    # Note: using (-np.inf, np.inf) as bounds as expected by current implementation
    vf1 = VectorFunction(vector_func, x0, jac='3-point', hess=BFGS(),
                         finite_diff_rel_step=None, finite_diff_jac_sparsity=None,
                         finite_diff_bounds=(-np.inf, np.inf), sparse_jacobian=None, workers=None)
    
    # Test with workers=1 (single worker) - using callable hessian
    vf2 = VectorFunction(vector_func, x0, jac='3-point', hess=BFGS(),
                         finite_diff_rel_step=None, finite_diff_jac_sparsity=None,
                         finite_diff_bounds=(-np.inf, np.inf), sparse_jacobian=None, workers=1)
    
    # Test with workers=2 (multiple workers) - using callable hessian
    vf3 = VectorFunction(vector_func, x0, jac='3-point', hess=BFGS(),
                         finite_diff_rel_step=None, finite_diff_jac_sparsity=None,
                         finite_diff_bounds=(-np.inf, np.inf), sparse_jacobian=None, workers=2)
    
    # Test that all work and produce the same results
    J1 = vf1.jac()
